artifacts.description: feat(kernel): through-all extent for extrude cuts

acceptance_criteria: `pub enum ThroughDirection { Normal, Reversed, Both }` and a new variant `Extent::ThroughAll(ThroughDirection)`, documented. `Normal` goes along the workplane normal, `Reversed` against it, `Both` both ways.

`extrude_feature` accepts `Extent::ThroughAll` only with `ExtrudeMode::Cut`. It replaces the extent with a finite one that reaches past the target in the chosen direction (for example `Distance(±L)` or `Symmetric(2L)`, with `L` = distance between the face and target bounding-box centers + half of each box diagonal + 1). The doc comment explains the bound.

Errors, each with a test and never a panic: `Kernel::extrude` with `Extent::ThroughAll` (no target to measure); `ThroughAll` with `NewSolid`, `Join` or `Intersect`; a through-all cut that removes nothing: the result volume equals the target volume within a relative 1e-9 (for example, `Normal` from the top face pointing away from the body). The message says the cut misses the target.

Tests on a target `make_box((0, 0, 0), (40, 25, 100))` with a circle of radius 5 centered at (20, 12.5) on an XY workplane, volumes within a relative 1e-6: origin (0, 0, 100), `Reversed`: volume 100000 − 2500π ≈ 92146.0184, face count 7; origin (0, 0, 110) (above the body), `Reversed`: same volume and face count; origin (0, 0, 50), `Both`: same volume and face count; origin (0, 0, 50), `Normal`: blind hole from z = 50 to 100, volume 100000 − 1250π ≈ 96073.0092, face count 8; `Workplane::YZ` with a circle of radius 5 at (u, v) = (12.5, 50), `Normal`: a hole along x through all 40, volume 100000 − 1000π ≈ 96858.4073, face count 7.
No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
